title: Notification system design
idea: A notification system turns domain events into messages on the right channels; five patterns split that job so each part changes without touching the rest.

analogy.text: A hotel front desk: news arrives, a clerk checks the do-not-disturb list and the hour, picks a note or a call, and redials if the line is busy.
analogy.breaks: A clerk improvises; each class here does one fixed job.

points: Observer decouples the order code: it publishes events and never names a channel.
Chain of Responsibility runs opt-out, quiet hours and dedup; any rule may veto.
A Strategy picks channels; a Factory builds them; a Decorator adds retry to each.
In interviews, justify each pattern by the change it absorbs, not just its name.

hero.title: One order event through five patterns

steps.caption: At startup `ChannelFactory` builds one channel per type and wraps each in `Retrying`.
Observer: `OrderEvents` pushes each note to every subscriber. It knows no channel.
Chain of Responsibility: each rule may block the note with a reason, or pass it on.
A veto ends the flow and is logged with its reason: opted out, quiet hours or duplicate.
Strategy: the policy chooses channels. Urgent notes get SMS and push; others get email.
The service sends through the wrapped channel. It sees only the `Channel` interface.
Decorator: SMS times out once and `Retrying` tries again. The service never sees the failure.
Each box changes alone: a new rule touches the chain; a new channel, the enum, factory and policy.

code.title: The problem: welded in
code.caption: Notification code lives inside the order service. Every new rule, channel or event edits this method.

walk.text: Order logic and notifying share one method. Neither can change or be tested alone.
The opt-out check returns silently. Support cannot tell why `bob` got nothing.
An if-else on strings picks the channel. A typo compiles and fails at runtime.
Push was never wired in, so the message is dropped: see the output.
No dedup: the same event sends the same email twice.
No retry, and each new event type copies the whole block.

code.title: The fix: five patterns
code.caption: Each pattern owns one reason to change. The service only wires them together.

walk.text: Observer: order code publishes a `Note`. Adding an audit listener needs no edit here.
Chain of Responsibility: the first rule that blocks returns its reason; else the next runs.
Dedup runs last, so vetoes stay unmarked. It marks before sending, so failed sends still count as sent.
Strategy: swap `UrgencyPolicy` for a per-user preference policy without touching the service.
Factory: an exhaustive `switch` on the `enum`; a new type will not compile until handled.
Decorator: retry wraps any channel and rethrows after the last attempt.
The service is short glue: check, pick, send. It depends only on interfaces.

pitfalls: Listeners that throw stop later listeners in a plain loop; catch per listener or dispatch asynchronously.
Putting dedup before opt-out marks blocked notes as sent; later legitimate sends are wrongly skipped.
Retrying a non-idempotent send without an id can deliver duplicates; pass a message id downstream.

quiz.q: Product asks for WhatsApp as a new channel. In the fixed design, what must change?
options: `NotificationService` and every rule in the chain
Only `Retrying`, since it wraps every channel
quiz.why: Creation lives in the factory, keyed by the enum, and a `ChannelPolicy` must choose WhatsApp. The service, rules and events stay untouched.

takeaway: Give each kind of change its own pattern; the service just wires them.
